scope: Condition, altitude, atmosphere and unit conventions for the reviewed historical G1 AFM cruise and cumulative-climb tables. Supersedes the open condition questions in afm-qualification-2026-09-12.json for the four gates below; every other blocker in that ledger still stands.
reviewMethod: Text extraction of the local primary PDF with pdftotext -layout, read against the printed page numbering. No new acquisition and no third-party transcription was used.

basis: PDF 31 / printed 1-15 defines Pressure Altitude and defines Standard Temperature as the temperature found at a given pressure altitude, decreasing approximately 2 C per 1000 ft.
PDF 366 / printed 5-8 'OAT for International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) Condition' is indexed by 'Press Alt Feet' and its ISA column is exactly 15 C minus 2 C per 1000 ft.
PDF 389 / printed 5-31 enroute climb tables are indexed by 'Press Alt FT'; PDF 473 / printed 5-115 takeoff climb tables are indexed by 'Press Alt Feet'.
The cruise table's own Delta ISA and OAT columns are the standard-temperature relation, which only closes if its altitude column is pressure altitude.
gates.residualInterpretation: The cruise heading itself prints only 'Alt FT'. Section 5 uses four spellings for the same quantity: 'Press Alt Feet', 'Press Alt FT', 'Altitude (ft)' and 'Alt FT'.

gates.resolution: The AFM's ISA is a dry perfect gas at 15 C and 29.92 inHg at sea level, and its standard temperature decreases 2 C per 1000 ft of pressure altitude. That 2 C per 1000 ft rule, not the true 1.98 C per 1000 ft lapse rate, reproduces every reviewed OAT column below 28,000 ft.
basis: PDF 30 / printed 1-14 defines ISA; PDF 31 / printed 1-15 defines Standard Temperature as decreasing approximately 4 F (2 C) per 1000 ft.
Reviewed cruise OAT at Delta ISA 0 is 5 C at 5,000 ft and -15 C at 15,000 ft, both exactly 15 - 2 per 1000.
The ISA cumulative-climb column on PDF 425 / printed 5-67 is exactly 15, 11, 7, 3, -1, -5, -9, -13, -17, -21, -25, -29, -33, -37 at 0 through 26,000 ft.
At 26,000 ft the reviewed table prints -37 C, which follows the 2 C per 1000 ft rule and not the true lapse rate's -36.48 C.
gates.recordedInconsistency: Every reviewed 28,000-ft entry is exactly 1 C warmer than the 2 C per 1000 ft rule: cruise prints -20/-30/-40/-50 C for Delta ISA +20/+10/0/-10 where the rule gives -21/-31/-41/-51, the ISA climb table prints -40 where the rule gives -41, and the ISA+10 climb tables print -30 where the rule gives -31. The general PDF 366 / printed 5-8 chart prints -41 C at 28,000 ft. The true 1.98 C per 1000 ft lapse rate gives -40.44 C, which rounds to the tables' -40. The offset is uniform across the whole 28,000-ft block rather than a single typo. Preserve both printed statements; the earlier -40 versus -41 conflict is explained but not eliminated.
gates.residualInterpretation: PDF 364 / printed 5-6 states the section's charts cover -20 C to 40 C ambient, yet the reviewed cruise and climb tables publish -50 C entries and the takeoff climb tables grid -40 C to 50 C. That statement does not bound the reviewed rows.

gates.resolution: Gear UP and flaps UP are used for cruise comparisons as a recorded inference, not a printed condition.
basis: PDF 363 / printed 5-5 states all data are based on published normal procedures.
PDF 364 / printed 5-6 states flap position and thrust setting technique are noted with each table.

The Cruise Performance section beginning at PDF 433 / printed 5-75 carries no Conditions block: only the '** MCT' and '* Max Range Cruise (No Wind)' legends. The preceding page is a cumulative-climb table.
The AFM labels its one non-clean set explicitly as 'Gear UP, Flaps 50%' at PDF 473 / printed 5-115 with a full Conditions block, so unlabelled tables are not that configuration.

PDF 348 / printed 4-22 normal takeoff retracts the gear with positive rate and the flaps at 115 KIAS; the enroute climb and cumulative climb Conditions blocks on PDF 388 and PDF 420 state gear UP and flaps UP.
gates.residualInterpretation: Cruise configuration is never printed in the reviewed cruise section. Treat gear/flap position as an assumption of any cruise comparison.

gates.resolution: Neither cruise anti-ice state nor bleed extraction is printed. Anti-ice OFF is used as a recorded assumption; installed bleed flow remains unknown.
basis: PDF 349 / printed 4-23 cruise checklist lists only Thrust Lever A/R, Ice Protection A/R and EIS MONITOR. It states no gear, flap, anti-ice or bleed setting.
The climb Conditions blocks state Anti-ice OFF (PDF 388, PDF 420 and the ice-contaminated equivalents); the cruise section states nothing.

Takeoff provides separate N1 schedules for Engine Anti-Ice OFF and ON (PDF 380 / Figure 5-2 and PDF 381 / Figure 5-3), so anti-ice measurably changes N1 for a given thrust. No equivalent cruise distinction is published.

The BLEED switch appears only in preflight verification and abnormal/emergency procedures, selecting FRESH air rather than scheduling engine bleed. The Bleed Bias Valve is required for all kinds of operation (PDF 67 / printed 2-31), so bleed extraction is continuous in normal cruise and is not pilot-scheduled.
The acquired EASA engine TCDS gives a maximum HP bleed flow of 40 lb/min. That is a limit, not the cruise extraction, and it is not a percentage thrust penalty.
gates.residualInterpretation: A standard day at the reviewed conditions is not an icing condition and ice protection is A/R, which makes anti-ice OFF the probable intended basis. It remains an inference. The model's 4 percent bleed thrust loss is an estimate with no source backing.

basis: The reviewed cruise tables print Specific Range in 'Nm/10 U.S. Gal' beside 'Fuel Flow GPH' in the same table.
Arithmetic agrees: 268 KTAS / 114 GPH gives 23.5 versus the printed 23.6 Nm per 10 US gal, and 295 / 99 gives 29.8 versus the printed 29.9.
Cumulative climb tables print 'Fuel (U.S. gal)' alongside 'Fuel (lb)', and Section 5's conversion chart is 'Fuel Quantity Conversion - U.S. Gallons to Liters' (printed 5-10).
PDF 33 / printed 1-17 defines GPH only as gallons per hour and does not itself state the gallon.
gates.residualInterpretation: This resolves the AFM only. The public dashboard's 'Engine 1 gal/Hr' caption remains unqualified, and the September 12 ledger's null qualified US-gph for that source still stands.

unchangedBlockers: The reviewed rows remain same-source calibration candidates; eligibleForCalibration and eligibleForIndependentValidation stay false.
Sensor, transcription and model-target uncertainty and any pass tolerance remain unestablished. Printed resolution is not a tolerance.
The 600 fitting candidate / 220 whole-condition ISA+10 same-source check allocation is unchanged, with zero independent validation rows.
These 27 transcription reviews plus these convention resolutions do not qualify the full 820-row corpus.
Loading and CG applicability for the reviewed rows remain unresolved; the printed 6,000 lb is a table condition, not a reviewed mass/CG state.
The 100.4 percent MCT N1 row at 28,000 ft still exceeds the model's estimated 100 percent endpoint, and the 104.7 percent limit is not a replacement FADEC or TLA schedule.
The 28,000-ft cumulative-climb endpoint's 32 US gal and 226 lb still do not reconcile at the nominal 6.76 lb per US gallon with simple rounding.
The landing revision and applicability discrepancy remains open.
